title: 1. Everything uploaded
see: Function names, file and line, source code around the line. Stack is complete: compare_players ← qsort ← Leaderboard::winner ← finish_match ← main.
why: This is how it should look. Sentry found a file with the same Debug ID for every image in the dump.

title: 2. Nothing uploaded
see: Processing Error: “A required debug information file was missing”. Frames are crashlab +0x15f4 <unknown>. The issue is called “qsort”, because it is the only name Sentry could find.
why: The dump has only addresses. Without the PDB there is nothing to translate them, and without the EXE Sentry can't even walk the stack properly, so some frames are just guesses (scan).
fix: sentry-cli debug-files check crashlab.pdb   # Debug ID must be the one from the error
sentry-cli debug-files upload --include-sources -o ORG -p PROJECT ./symbols
Send the crash again, or Reprocess the issue (needs stored minidumps)

title: 3. Symbols from another build
uploaded: crashlab.exe + crashlab.pdb, but from a rebuild of the same commit
see: Same error as in 2. In Project Settings → Debug Files there IS a crashlab.pdb, and the customer says “but I uploaded it”.
why: Name does not matter, the Debug ID does. Every link gives a new GUID to the PDB, even when the code did not change. Rebuilt on another machine = different file for Sentry.
fix: Compare the Debug ID in the event error with: sentry-cli debug-files check crashlab.pdb
Ask for the PDB from the exact build that was shipped (CI artifact, symbol server)
Fix the pipeline: upload symbols in the same job that builds the release

title: 4. PDB only, no EXE
see: Names and lines are there, but the stack has extra frames that never happened (__scrt_release_startup_lock, truncl$thunk…) and the same “missing” error still shows.
why: On 64-bit Windows the unwind info lives in the EXE/DLL, not in the PDB. Without it Sentry scans the stack memory for anything that looks like a return address. Images Loaded shows debug: found, unwind: missing.
fix: Upload the binaries too: sentry-cli debug-files upload ./bin   # .exe and .dll next to .pdb
sentry-cli debug-files check crashlab.exe   # must say: Contained debug information: unwind

title: 5. EXE only, no PDB
see: The stack has the right number of frames, but every crashlab frame is <unknown>. Error “missing” again.
why: The opposite of 4. The EXE gives unwind info (stack is walked correctly) but has no function names. Images Loaded: debug: missing, unwind: found.
fix: Upload the PDB with the same Debug ID

title: 6. Stripped (public) PDB
see: Function names, but no file, no line number, no inlined frames. No error at all.
why: A stripped PDB keeps only public symbols. Sentry thinks all is fine, because the file with this Debug ID was found. Same happens with strip -g on Linux when only the symbol table is left.
fix: sentry-cli debug-files check crashlab.pdb   # a full one is several MB, stripped is small
Upload the full private PDB from the build (link with /DEBUG:FULL)

title: 7. No source code
see: Perfect names and lines, but frames don't expand: no code around the line.
why: Debug info has file names and line numbers, not the text of the files. Source context comes from a source bundle (or Source Link for .NET/Portable PDB).
fix: sentry-cli debug-files upload --include-sources ./symbols
or: sentry-cli debug-files bundle-sources crashlab.pdb, then upload the .src.zip
The build machine must have the sources at the same paths as in the PDB

title: 8. No system symbols
uploaded: all crashlab files. But “Microsoft” is removed from Built-in Repositories of the project
see: Only 2 frames: compare_players and ucrtbase <unknown>. main and the rest of the stack are gone. No error.
why: The crash goes through ucrtbase.dll (qsort calls our callback). Sentry can't unwind through a system DLL it has no file for, so the stack walk stops there. System files are never reported as “required”.
fix: Project Settings → Debug Files → Built-in Repositories → add Microsoft (and others the app needs)
For OEM / driver DLLs that are on no public server: customer adds a Custom Repository or uploads them

title: 9. Truncated minidump
uploaded: all crashlab files. The dump file itself was cut at 60 KB
see: One frame only (it comes from the CPU registers), no other threads. No error.
why: Symbols are fine, the dump is not: the stack memory is missing from the file. Happens with size limits on proxies, disk full, process killed while writing.
fix: Download the attachment and look at the size; compare with a healthy dump
Check upload limits (Sentry takes up to 40 MB compressed, a proxy in the middle often less)

title: 10. Not a minidump
uploaded: all crashlab files. The uploaded “dump” is a text file
see: Nothing in Issues. The endpoint answers HTTP 400 {"detail":"invalid minidump"}, the event is dropped.
why: The minidump endpoint checks the MDMP magic bytes. Customers hit this with a wrong form field name, gzip without the header, or a full Windows dump in another format.
fix: Stats → Invalid shows the dropped events
curl the endpoint by hand with the same file to see the answer
Form field must be upload_file_minidump

title: 11. Bonus: the bad value is in a register
uploaded: crashlab.exe + crashlab.pdb + source bundle. Another bug this time: average_score(total, games) with games = 0
see: EXCEPTION_INT_DIVIDE_BY_ZERO in average_score, crashlab.cpp:86. Expand the top frame, Registers: rax = 0x3d7 (total), r8 = 0 (games).
why: The code is mov r8d,edx / mov eax,ecx / cdq / idiv r8d. The divisor came in edx and was moved to r8, so r8 = 0 is the bad argument. rdx is 0 too, but only because cdq overwrote it. Sentry shows raw registers of the top frame, it does not tell you which one is which argument.
fix: Registers are exact only for the crashing frame
Windows x64 args: rcx, rdx, r8, r9. Linux/macOS: rdi, rsi, rdx, rcx, r8, r9. Valid at function entry, later the code may reuse them
To map a register to a variable you need the disassembly: dumpbin /disasm, objdump -d, or a debugger with the dump
